title: A Comfortable Seat
lines: Tom rides his bike to school each day.
The way to school is long and bumpy.
But the seat on his bike was hard as a rock.
"It is not comfortable," he told Mom.
By the third hill he had to stand up.
First Tom taped a soft rag on the seat.
It felt much better in the yard.
But the rag slid off on the first hill.
Then he tried a folded towel and some cord.
That slid off as well and fell in the mud.
So they went to the bike shop to look.
One seat was soft but very breakable.
"That one will crack," said the man in the shop.
Tom picked a thick one that was unbreakable.
It cost a bit more, but it will not break.
Mom handed him the tools to fix it on.
Tom took the old seat off and set the new one on.
He sat on it and gave a big grin.
Now his long rides are enjoyable.
Tom rides all the way to school and back.

questions.ask: What two things did Tom try before the bike shop?
questions.listenFor: A soft rag taped on, then a folded towel and cord. Both slid off.

questions.ask: Why did Tom pick the thick seat?
questions.listenFor: It was unbreakable. The other one was breakable - able to be broken. Point at the -able ending doing that job.

questions.ask: What is something of yours you wish were unbreakable? Why?
questions.listenFor: A toy, a cup, a tablet. The why is the part worth waiting for.
